question: Should generic tool-progress intent become a permanent public reply-payload plugin-SDK contract, or remain a narrow internal bundled-runtime seam?
rationale: The PR adds public exports with lasting third-party compatibility obligations, so code review cannot safely choose the permanent owner boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Internalize the seam
options.body: Keep typed Codex-to-Slack progress behavior behind the narrow bundled internal boundary and avoid expanding the public plugin SDK.

options.title: Approve public contract
options.body: Keep the public constant and predicate, document their semantics, and add compatibility-focused contract coverage.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers choose a supported cross-plugin progress ownership model.

recommendation.title: Internalize the seam
recommendation.body: Keep typed Codex-to-Slack progress behavior behind the narrow bundled internal boundary and avoid expanding the public plugin SDK.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the native Slack block path, and the decision spans that surface plus the repository's plugin architecture boundary.
